original_context: Nico does not speak the truth.
Nico does not spark a conversation.
Nico does not spark heated debates.
Anyone who faces backlash or speaks the truth will spark a conversation.
For all humans, if they either challenge the status quo or question authority, then they think critically.
Anyone who holds unpopular opinions will either face backlash or inspire followers.
Anyone who holds unpopular opinions will express unconventional views.
Anyone who challenges the status quo will push boundaries.
If someone fosters critical thinking, then they encourage discussion and push boundaries.
Nico either fosters critical thinking or creates controversial art, but not both.
Anyone who expresses unconventional views or gains notoriety will attract attention.
conclusion: If Nico creates controversial art, then he will spark heated debates and gain notoriety.

qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.mistake: The FOL uses exclusive or (⊕) but the natural language does not specify that only one of the conditions can be true. It incorrectly suggests an inclusive or.

openai/gpt-5-mini.mistake: Minor ambiguity: ∀x ((p_13(x) ⊕ p_4(x)) → p_5(x)) uses exclusive OR but the NL “if x either challenges the status quo or questions authority” is ambiguous about exclusivity. This is a small mismatch in exclusivity interpretation, not a clear semantic error.

openai/gpt-5-mini.mistake: The formula ∀x ((p_13(x) ⊕ p_4(x)) → p_5(x)) uses exclusive OR (⊕), forcing exactly one of p_13 or p_4 to hold.
